properties.displayName: ITD-A001 Directory replication (DCSync) by an account that is not a domain controller
properties.description:
Detects directory replication requests for password data from a user account.
Domain controllers replicate with their computer accounts. A user account that
exercises the replication rights is either the Entra Connect AD DS connector,
which is excluded, or someone pulling password hashes, including the krbtgt
key, without touching a domain controller's disk.
Requires Audit Directory Service Access and an auditing entry on the domain
root for the replication rights.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1003.006

False positives:
- Entra Connect connector accounts with a custom name. Add them to the exclusion.
- Identity security tools that read replication data with a dedicated account. Document and exclude them by SID.

Triage:
- Treat as critical until proven otherwise; an attacker who replicated the krbtgt key can forge tickets for any account.
- Identify the source of the logon session (SubjectLogonId, event 4624 on the same domain controller) to find the requesting host.
- If not legitimate, isolate the source host, reset the account, and plan a double krbtgt reset and a reset of all Tier-0 credentials.

Preventive controls:
- hybrid-workplace-automation · Get-ADTier0Exposure.ps1 finding ReplicationRights (no replication rights outside domain controllers)

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-A001 v1.0.0
properties.query:
// DS-Replication-Get-Changes, -Get-Changes-All and -Get-Changes-In-Filtered-Set
let ReplicationRights = dynamic(["1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2", "1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2", "89e95b76-444d-4c62-991a-0facbeda640c"]);
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4662
| where ObjectServer =~ "DS"
| where AccountType != "Machine" and not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| where Properties has_any (ReplicationRights)
// Entra Connect AD DS connector account (default naming). Add custom connector accounts here.
| where not(SubjectUserName startswith "MSOL_")
| summarize Events = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by Computer, SubjectAccount, SubjectUserName, SubjectUserSid, SubjectLogonId

properties.displayName: ITD-A002 Domain trust created, removed or modified
properties.description:
Detects the creation, removal or modification of a trust between this domain
and another domain or forest. A new or weakened trust (for example SID
filtering disabled) opens a path for principals of the other side into this
domain. Trust changes are rare, so each one should match a planned change.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1484.002

False positives:
- Planned trust changes during mergers, migrations or the decommissioning of a domain.
- Line-of-business software that recreates a trust it depends on. Verify with the vendor and document it.

Triage:
- Is there a change request for this trust and partner domain?
- Check direction, type and SID filtering in EventData. A trust without SID filtering is especially dangerous.
- Correlate with logons of the acting account in the hour before the change.
- If not legitimate, remove the trust and investigate the acting account as compromised.

Preventive controls:
- hybrid-workplace-automation · Get-ADTier0Exposure.ps1 (Tier-0 membership limited to the accounts that need it)

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-A002 v1.0.0
properties.query:
// 4706 trust created, 4707 trust removed, 4716 trust information modified
SecurityEvent
| where EventID in (4706, 4707, 4716)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, EventID, Activity, SubjectAccount, SubjectUserName, SubjectUserSid, DomainName, DomainSid, EventData

properties.displayName: ITD-A003 Member added to a Tier-0 group
properties.description:
Detects additions to the built-in privileged groups of Active Directory:
Administrators, Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, Account,
Server, Print and Backup Operators, Group Policy Creator Owners, Key Admins and
Enterprise Key Admins. Groups are matched by well-known SID and RID, so the
rule also works in domains with localised group names.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1098.007

False positives:
- Approved admin onboarding. With a tiered admin model these changes are rare and ticketed.
- Members added temporarily for a maintenance task. They should also be removed again (event 4729, 4733, 4757).

Triage:
- Is there an approved request for this membership?
- Who made the change, and from which session? A change made by an account that is itself new to Tier 0 is a strong signal.
- If not legitimate, remove the member, disable the account and investigate the acting account.

Preventive controls:
- hybrid-workplace-automation · Get-ADTier0Exposure.ps1 (review of PrivilegedAccounts.csv)

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-A003 v1.0.0

properties.displayName: ITD-A004 Kerberoasting: RC4 service tickets for many service accounts
properties.description:
Detects an account that requests RC4-encrypted Kerberos service tickets for at
least five different user-based service accounts within an hour. Kerberoasting
requests service tickets on purpose to crack the service account's password
offline; RC4 is requested because it cracks much faster than AES. In domains
that have moved to AES, even a single RC4 request for a privileged service
account is worth an alert; lower the threshold accordingly.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1558.003

False positives:
- Legacy applications and appliances that only support RC4.
- Vulnerability scanners and inventory tools that enumerate services. Document and exclude their accounts.

Triage:
- Which host requested the tickets (SourceIp), and is the requesting account expected to talk to these services?
- Are any of the requested service accounts privileged? Those passwords must be changed first.
- If not legitimate, isolate the host, reset the passwords of the requested service accounts and move them to gMSAs.

Preventive controls:
- hybrid-workplace-automation · Get-ADTier0Exposure.ps1 finding Kerberoastable (no SPNs on privileged accounts, gMSAs for services)

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-A004 v1.0.0
properties.query:
let Threshold = 5;
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4769
| parse EventData with * 'TicketEncryptionType">' TicketEncryptionType "<" *
| parse EventData with * 'Name="Status">' TicketStatus "<" *
| where TicketEncryptionType =~ "0x17" and TicketStatus =~ "0x0"
// Computer accounts and krbtgt have long random passwords and are not worth cracking.
| where not(ServiceName endswith "$") and ServiceName !~ "krbtgt"
| extend SourceIp = trim_start(@"::ffff:", IpAddress)
| summarize ServiceCount = dcount(ServiceName), Services = make_set(ServiceName, 50), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by TargetUserName, SourceIp
| where ServiceCount >= Threshold

properties.displayName: ITD-A005 Password spray against Active Directory
properties.description:
Detects one source address that fails Kerberos pre-authentication or NTLM
logon with a wrong password for at least ten different accounts within an
hour. On the domain controllers, the rule sees Kerberos pre-authentication
failures (4771) and failed logons that reach a domain controller directly,
for example LDAP binds from VPN gateways, firewalls or web portals (4625).
NTLM failures that a member server passes through to a domain controller
(4776) carry no source address and are not covered.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1110.003

False positives:
- Terminal servers, VPN concentrators and proxies that authenticate many users and forward their typos.
- Services configured with an old password for several accounts.

Triage:
- Which system owns the source address? For a VPN or firewall, find the external address in its own logs.
- Did any of the targeted accounts log on successfully from the same source afterwards (event 4624)?
- If not legitimate, block the source, reset the passwords of accounts with a later successful logon and review them for misuse.

Preventive controls:
- hybrid-workplace-automation · Get-ADTier0Exposure.ps1 findings PasswordNeverExpires and PasswordOld for privileged accounts

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-A005 v1.0.0
properties.query:
let Threshold = 10;
SecurityEvent
// 4625 with 0xC000006A = wrong password (NTLM), 4771 with 0x18 = wrong password (Kerberos pre-authentication)
| where (EventID == 4625 and SubStatus =~ "0xc000006a") or (EventID == 4771 and Status =~ "0x18")
| extend SourceIp = trim_start(@"::ffff:", IpAddress)
| where isnotempty(SourceIp) and SourceIp !in ("-", "127.0.0.1", "::1")
| summarize TargetedAccounts = dcount(TargetUserName), Failures = count(), SampleAccounts = make_set(TargetUserName, 20),
    ReportingHosts = make_set(Computer, 10), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by SourceIp
| where TargetedAccounts >= Threshold

properties.description:
Detects clearing of the Windows Security event log. Attackers clear the log
on domain controllers and servers to remove the traces of logons, privilege
use and persistence. Clearing the log manually is rarely part of normal
operations, and the clearing itself is always logged.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1070.001

False positives:
- Rebuilding a server or a lab system. Exclude lab hosts by name.

Triage:
- Is there a reason for the clearing, such as a rebuild?
- What happened on the host just before the clearing? Events already forwarded to the SIEM survive the clearing.
- If not legitimate, treat the host and the acting account as compromised.

Preventive controls:
- Forward security events to the SIEM in near real time, so clearing the local log does not remove the evidence.

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-A006 v1.0.0
properties.query:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 1102
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Activity, SubjectAccount, SubjectUserName, SubjectUserSid, SubjectDomainName, EventData

properties.displayName: ITD-A007 Tier-0 account signed in to a host outside Tier 0
properties.description:
Detects interactive, remote interactive, batch, service, cached and
NewCredentials logons of Tier-0 accounts on hosts that are not Tier-0 assets.
These logon types leave reusable credentials in memory. One Domain Admin
logon on a workstation or member server turns a compromise of that host into
a compromise of the domain; the tiered admin model exists to prevent exactly
this. Accounts come from the watchlist Tier0Accounts (SearchKey =
sAMAccountName), hosts from the watchlist Tier0Hosts (SearchKey = host name
without domain).

MITRE ATT&CK: T1078.002

False positives:
- Privileged access workstations or jump servers that are missing from the Tier0Hosts watchlist.
- Scheduled tasks or services on member servers that still run as a Domain Admin. These are findings, not noise; move them to a service account with the rights they need.

Triage:
- Which host, which logon type, and who used the account at that time?
- Is the host a privileged access workstation that is missing from the watchlist? If so, add it.
- If not, treat the account's credentials as exposed on that host. Check the host for compromise, then rotate the account's password and investigate how it got there.

Preventive controls:
- hybrid-workplace-automation · Get-ADTier0Exposure.ps1 findings PrivilegedAccountDelegable and ComputerInPrivilegedGroup (Protected Users, sensitive accounts)
- Authentication policies and silos, or user rights assignments that deny Tier-0 logons outside Tier 0

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-A007 v1.0.0
properties.query:
let Tier0Accounts = _GetWatchlist('Tier0Accounts') | project Account = tolower(tostring(SearchKey));
let Tier0Hosts = _GetWatchlist('Tier0Hosts') | project HostName = tolower(tostring(SearchKey));
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4624
// 2 interactive, 4 batch, 5 service, 9 NewCredentials, 10 remote interactive, 11 cached interactive
| where LogonType in (2, 4, 5, 9, 10, 11)
| extend Account = tolower(TargetUserName), HostName = tolower(tostring(split(Computer, ".")[0]))
| where Account in (Tier0Accounts)
| where HostName !in (Tier0Hosts)
| summarize Logons = count(), LogonTypes = make_set(LogonTypeName, 10), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by Computer, HostName, TargetAccount, TargetUserName, IpAddress

properties.displayName: ITD-E001 Conditional Access policy created, changed or deleted
properties.description:
Detects every change to a Conditional Access policy. Attackers with a privileged
session weaken Conditional Access to keep access: they switch a policy off,
add their account or a trusted location to the exclusions, or remove the MFA
requirement. The query adds the old and new state and flags changed exclusions
so the analyst sees at a glance whether the change weakened the policy.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1556.009

False positives:
- Planned changes by the identity team. Compare with the change calendar; deployments from a pipeline show the automation app as actor.
- Microsoft-managed policies, which are changed by Microsoft and show a Microsoft service as actor.

Triage:
- Was the change planned and approved? Ask the actor through a channel other than their mailbox.
- Did the change weaken the policy? Look at NewState (disabled or report-only) and ExclusionsChanged.
- Check the actor's sign-ins of the last 24 hours for unfamiliar locations, devices or risk.
- If the change is not legitimate, revert it from the last export of the policies and revoke the actor's sessions.

Preventive controls:
- id-hub Level 3 · zero standing privilege for the Conditional Access Administrator role (PIM with authentication context)
- id-hub Level 3 · CA301 phishing-resistant MFA for admins

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-E001 v1.0.0
properties.query:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName in~ ("Add conditional access policy", "Update conditional access policy", "Delete conditional access policy")
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend Actor = coalesce(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName))
| extend ActorIpAddress = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend PolicyName = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName), PolicyId = tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
| extend ModifiedProperties = TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties
| extend OldPolicy = parse_json(tostring(ModifiedProperties[0].oldValue)), NewPolicy = parse_json(tostring(ModifiedProperties[0].newValue))
| extend OldState = tostring(OldPolicy.state), NewState = tostring(NewPolicy.state)
| extend ExclusionsChanged = tostring(OldPolicy.conditions.users.excludeUsers) != tostring(NewPolicy.conditions.users.excludeUsers)
    or tostring(OldPolicy.conditions.users.excludeGroups) != tostring(NewPolicy.conditions.users.excludeGroups)
    or tostring(OldPolicy.conditions.users.excludeRoles) != tostring(NewPolicy.conditions.users.excludeRoles)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, PolicyName, PolicyId, OldState, NewState, ExclusionsChanged, Actor, ActorIpAddress, ModifiedProperties, CorrelationId

properties.displayName: ITD-E002 New credential added to an application or service principal
properties.description:
Detects a new client secret or certificate on an app registration or service
principal. A credential on an application with high Graph permissions is a
persistent backdoor: it survives password resets and MFA changes of every
user and signs in without Conditional Access for users. The query compares
the number of keys before and after the change, so it only fires when a key
was added.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1098.001

False positives:
- Planned secret or certificate rotation by the application owner or a rotation automation.
- New app registrations, which receive their first credential shortly after creation.

Triage:
- Is the actor an owner of the application, and was a rotation due?
- What permissions does the application hold? A credential on an app with Mail, Files, Directory or RoleManagement permissions is critical.
- Check the service principal sign-ins after the change for unfamiliar IP addresses.
- If the credential is not legitimate, remove it, review the application's activity since the change and rotate the remaining credentials.

Preventive controls:
- id-hub Level 2 · application credentials (named owners, certificates or federated credentials instead of secrets)
- id-hub Level 3 · CA306 workload identities only from trusted locations

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-E002 v1.0.0
properties.query:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName has_any ("Add service principal", "Certificates and secrets management")
| where Result =~ "success"
| mv-apply Target = TargetResources on (
    where tostring(Target.type) in~ ("Application", "ServicePrincipal")
    | extend TargetType = tostring(Target.type), AppName = tostring(Target.displayName), AppObjectId = tostring(Target.id), Properties = Target.modifiedProperties
  )
| mv-apply Property = Properties on (
    where tostring(Property.displayName) =~ "KeyDescription"
    | extend NewKeys = parse_json(tostring(Property.newValue)), OldKeys = parse_json(tostring(Property.oldValue))
  )
| where array_length(NewKeys) > array_length(OldKeys)
| extend Actor = coalesce(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName))
| extend ActorIpAddress = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, TargetType, AppName, AppObjectId, NewKeys, Actor, ActorIpAddress, CorrelationId

properties.displayName: ITD-E003 Consent to an application with high-risk permissions
properties.description:
Detects user or admin consent to an application that requests access to mail,
files or the directory. Consent phishing does not steal a password: the victim
grants a malicious application a token that keeps working after a password
reset, and Conditional Access for users does not apply to the application's
later access. The list of high-risk permissions is a starting point; extend it
with the permissions that matter in your tenant.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1528

False positives:
- Admin consent for a reviewed line-of-business or SaaS application during onboarding.
- Users consenting to verified-publisher applications that the tenant allows.

Triage:
- Is the application known, from a verified publisher and used by others in the tenant?
- Did the user receive an email or chat message with a link shortly before the consent?
- Which permissions were granted, and did the application access mail or files after the consent?
- If malicious, revoke the consent, disable the service principal, revoke the user's sessions and search for the same application in other users' consents.

Preventive controls:
- id-hub Level 1 · application consent (user consent limited, admin consent workflow)

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-E003 v1.0.0
properties.query:
let HighRiskPermissions = dynamic(["Mail.Read", "Mail.ReadWrite", "Mail.Send", "MailboxSettings.ReadWrite", "Files.Read.All", "Files.ReadWrite.All", "Sites.Read.All", "Sites.ReadWrite.All", "Notes.Read.All", "User.ReadWrite.All", "Directory.ReadWrite.All", "Application.ReadWrite.All", "AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All", "RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory", "full_access_as_app", "EWS.AccessAsUser.All"]);
AuditLogs
| where OperationName =~ "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| mv-apply Property = TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties on (
    summarize Props = make_bag(bag_pack(tostring(Property.displayName), trim(@'"', tostring(Property.newValue))))
  )
| extend Permissions = tostring(Props["ConsentAction.Permissions"]), IsAdminConsent = tostring(Props["ConsentContext.IsAdminConsent"])
| where Permissions has_any (HighRiskPermissions)
| extend AppName = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName), ServicePrincipalId = tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
| extend Actor = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), ActorIpAddress = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| project TimeGenerated, AppName, ServicePrincipalId, IsAdminConsent, Permissions, Actor, ActorIpAddress, CorrelationId

properties.displayName: ITD-E004 Directory role assigned outside Privileged Identity Management
properties.description:
Detects a permanent directory role assignment that was made directly instead
of through Privileged Identity Management. In a tenant that uses PIM, direct
assignments bypass approval, justification and time limits. An attacker with
a privileged session uses them to give a second account standing privilege
that survives the loss of the first.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1098.003

False positives:
- Break-glass accounts, which keep permanent Global Administrator by design.
- Tenants or roles that are not managed with PIM yet. Exclude those roles until they are.

Triage:
- Which role was assigned, and to whom? Global, Privileged Role and Privileged Authentication Administrator are critical.
- Was the assignment requested through the normal process?
- Check the actor's and the target's sign-ins and audit activity since the assignment.
- If not legitimate, remove the assignment, revoke both accounts' sessions and review what the target did with the role.

Preventive controls:
- id-hub Level 2 · PIM for all privileged roles
- id-hub Level 3 · zero standing privilege, PIM activation with authentication context

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-E004 v1.0.0
properties.query:
AuditLogs
| where Category =~ "RoleManagement"
| where OperationName =~ "Add member to role outside of PIM"
    or (OperationName =~ "Add member to role" and LoggedByService =~ "Core Directory" and Identity != "MS-PIM")
| where Result =~ "success"
| mv-apply Property = TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties on (
    summarize Props = make_bag(bag_pack(tostring(Property.displayName), trim(@'"', tostring(Property.newValue))))
  )
| extend RoleName = tostring(Props["Role.DisplayName"])
| extend TargetUser = tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName), TargetObjectId = tostring(TargetResources[0].id)
| extend Actor = coalesce(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName))
| extend ActorIpAddress = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, RoleName, TargetUser, TargetObjectId, Actor, ActorIpAddress, CorrelationId

properties.displayName: ITD-E005 Successful sign-in with the device code flow
properties.description:
Detects successful sign-ins that used the OAuth device code flow. Device code
phishing sends the victim a legitimate Microsoft sign-in page with a code the
attacker generated. The victim completes MFA, and the attacker's device
receives the tokens. Most users never need this flow, so every successful use
outside the known exceptions deserves a look.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1528

False positives:
- Admins who sign in to the Azure CLI or PowerShell on headless hosts.
- Meeting room devices and other input-constrained devices that are enrolled with a device code.

Triage:
- Does the user know the sign-in? Ask by phone or chat, not by email.
- Is the IP address or country unusual for the user, or different from the user's other sign-ins at the same time?
- Did the user receive a message with a code and a link to microsoft.com/devicelogin shortly before?
- If not legitimate, revoke the user's sessions and refresh tokens, and review mail and file access since the sign-in.

Preventive controls:
- id-hub Level 2 · CA209 block device code flow

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-E005 v1.0.0
properties.query:
SigninLogs
| where AuthenticationProtocol =~ "deviceCode" or OriginalTransferMethod =~ "deviceCodeFlow"
| where ResultType == "0"
| extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion), City = tostring(LocationDetails.city)
| extend DeviceOs = tostring(DeviceDetail.operatingSystem), DeviceCompliant = tostring(DeviceDetail.isCompliant)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, ResourceDisplayName, IPAddress, Country, City, DeviceOs, DeviceCompliant, UserAgent, ConditionalAccessStatus, CorrelationId

properties.displayName: ITD-E006 Authentication method registered after a risky sign-in
properties.description:
Detects the registration of a new authentication method within four hours
after a medium or high risk sign-in of the same user. After stealing a
password or a session, attackers register their own authenticator app or
phone number. From then on they pass MFA on their own, and resetting the
password no longer locks them out.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1098.005

False positives:
- A user who travels, gets flagged as risky and sets up a new phone on the same day.
- Risk detections from VPN or anonymising networks that the organisation uses.

Triage:
- Compare the IP address of the registration with the risky sign-in and the user's usual locations.
- Ask the user, by phone, whether they registered a new method.
- If not legitimate, delete the new method, revoke all sessions, reset the password and confirm the remaining methods with the user.

Preventive controls:
- id-hub Level 2 · CA206 security info registration only with MFA or from trusted locations
- id-hub Level 1 · Temporary Access Pass for onboarding and recovery

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-E006 v1.0.0
properties.query:
let RiskySignIns = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
    | where RiskLevelDuringSignIn in~ ("medium", "high")
    | project RiskyTime = TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName = tolower(UserPrincipalName), RiskLevelDuringSignIn, RiskyIpAddress = IPAddress;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where OperationName in~ ("User registered security info", "Admin registered security info", "User changed default security info")
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend UserPrincipalName = tolower(coalesce(tostring(TargetResources[0].userPrincipalName), tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName)))
| extend ActorIpAddress = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress), Detail = ResultReason
| join kind=inner RiskySignIns on UserPrincipalName
| where TimeGenerated between (RiskyTime .. (RiskyTime + 4h))
| summarize arg_max(RiskyTime, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, RiskyIpAddress) by TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, OperationName, Detail, ActorIpAddress, CorrelationId

properties.displayName: ITD-E007 Password spray against Microsoft Entra ID
properties.description:
Detects one IP address that fails to sign in to at least ten different
accounts within an hour with a wrong password or a smart lockout. Password
spraying tries one or two common passwords against many accounts to stay
below the lockout threshold. The result lists accounts that signed in
successfully from the same address in the same hour; those accounts are
likely compromised.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1110.003

False positives:
- Shared egress addresses (proxy, VPN, NAT) where many users mistype passwords at the start of the day.
- Misconfigured applications or devices that retry old passwords of several accounts.

Triage:
- Is the IP address your own egress or a known partner? If so, look for one client causing the failures.
- System.Collections.Specialized.OrderedDictionary
- For compromised accounts, reset the password, revoke sessions and check for new authentication methods (ITD-E006).

Preventive controls:
- id-hub Level 1 · CA101 block legacy authentication
- id-hub Level 2 · CA201 MFA for all users and apps

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-E007 v1.0.0
properties.query:
let FailureCodes = dynamic(["50126", "50053"]);
let Threshold = 10;
SigninLogs
| where ResultType in (FailureCodes) or ResultType == "0"
| summarize
    TargetedAccounts = dcountif(UserPrincipalName, ResultType in (FailureCodes)),
    Failures = countif(ResultType in (FailureCodes)),
    SampleAccounts = make_set_if(UserPrincipalName, ResultType in (FailureCodes), 20),
    SuccessfulAccounts = make_set_if(UserPrincipalName, ResultType == "0", 20),
    Apps = make_set(AppDisplayName, 10),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
    by IPAddress
| where TargetedAccounts >= Threshold
| extend SuccessCount = array_length(SuccessfulAccounts)

properties.displayName: ITD-E008 Sign-in attempt with a break-glass account
properties.description:
Detects every sign-in attempt, successful or not, with an emergency access
account. Break-glass accounts are excluded from Conditional Access and hold
permanent Global Administrator, so any use outside a declared emergency or a
scheduled test is an incident. The accounts are read from the watchlist
BreakGlassAccounts (SearchKey = user principal name).

MITRE ATT&CK: T1078.004

False positives:
- Scheduled tests of the emergency procedure. Announce them to the SOC beforehand.

Triage:
- Is there a declared emergency or a scheduled test? If not, treat it as an incident.
- System.Collections.Specialized.OrderedDictionary
- System.Collections.Specialized.OrderedDictionary

Preventive controls:
- id-hub Level 1 · at least two cloud-only break-glass accounts with passkeys or certificates, excluded only through one group
- id-hub Level 2 · alerting on break-glass use
- id-hub Level 3 · break-glass governance with regular tests

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-E008 v1.0.0
properties.query:
let BreakGlassAccounts = _GetWatchlist('BreakGlassAccounts') | project UserPrincipalName = tolower(tostring(SearchKey));
SigninLogs
| extend UserPrincipalName = tolower(UserPrincipalName)
| where UserPrincipalName in (BreakGlassAccounts)
| extend Country = tostring(LocationDetails.countryOrRegion), City = tostring(LocationDetails.city)
| project TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, ResultType, ResultDescription, AppDisplayName, IPAddress, Country, City, UserAgent, ConditionalAccessStatus, CorrelationId

properties.displayName: ITD-E009 Domain federation or authentication settings changed
properties.description:
Detects a change of the authentication type or the federation settings of a
domain in the tenant. An attacker who converts a domain to federated, or adds
a second token-signing certificate, can issue tokens for any user of that
domain from infrastructure they control, including MFA claims. Changes like
this are rare and should always be tied to a planned project.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1484.002

False positives:
- Planned migrations between federation and cloud authentication, and planned renewals of AD FS token-signing certificates.

Triage:
- Is there a change request for this domain?
- Compare the issuer URI and signing certificate in ModifiedProperties with your known federation servers.
- If not legitimate, revert the domain to managed authentication, revoke sessions of all users of the domain and investigate the actor.

Preventive controls:
- id-hub Level 3 · zero standing privilege for Global and Hybrid Identity Administrator

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-E009 v1.0.0
properties.query:
AuditLogs
| where OperationName in~ ("Set domain authentication", "Set federation settings on domain")
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend DomainName = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName)
| extend Actor = coalesce(tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName), tostring(InitiatedBy.app.displayName))
| extend ActorIpAddress = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress)
| extend ModifiedProperties = TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, DomainName, Actor, ActorIpAddress, ModifiedProperties, CorrelationId

properties.displayName: ITD-E010 Successful sign-in with legacy authentication
properties.description:
Detects accounts that signed in successfully with a legacy authentication
protocol such as IMAP, POP, SMTP AUTH or Exchange ActiveSync with basic
authentication. These protocols cannot do MFA, which makes them the preferred
target of password spraying. Once legacy authentication is blocked, every
success is either an exception you know about or a gap in the policy.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1078.004

False positives:
- Known exceptions such as multifunction printers that send mail through SMTP AUTH. Document them and exclude them by account.

Triage:
- Is the account a documented exception? If so, check that the exception still has an owner and an end date.
- If not, find out why the block policy did not apply (excluded user, report-only, other client type) and close the gap.
- Check the IP addresses for spraying activity (ITD-E007).

Preventive controls:
- id-hub Level 1 · CA101 block legacy authentication

Source: identity-threat-detections ITD-E010 v1.0.0
properties.query:
SigninLogs
| where ResultType == "0"
| where isnotempty(ClientAppUsed) and ClientAppUsed !in~ ("Browser", "Mobile Apps and Desktop clients")
| summarize SignIns = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), IpAddresses = make_set(IPAddress, 20), Apps = make_set(AppDisplayName, 10)
